name: LULA reward recycle confiscates and re-syncs the LULA/USDT pair reserve

classification.summary: The LULA token funds its referral reward payouts by confiscating liquidity from its own AMM pair. LULA.recycle(uint256) computes `maxTake = balanceOf[uniswapV2Pair] / 3`, moves `min(amount, maxTake)` LULA from the PancakeSwap LULA/USDT pair 0xf0b36389a12a28be1280c0ec2a4bbc76889d6a96 to the rental contract with an internal `_basicTransfer`, then calls `IUniswapV2Pair.sync()` so the pair adopts the reduced reserve. The pair's constant product is therefore reducible on the token side, at a caller-chosen moment, with no compensating movement on the USDT side, and the rental contract 0x377a015f44c3fdf71060e94648edc9e0316c7f1a exposes it to any account holding reward credit through a permissionless claimTeamReward(). The attacker flash-loaned 197,050,832.75 USDT, bought the entire LULA float out of the pair into the fee-exempt owner address so no buy tax or cooldown was recorded, then drove 41 claimTeamReward/recycle iterations that took the pair's remaining 24,022.132677570768 LULA while its USDT reserve stayed at 197.6M, and finally sold the recycled LULA back into the now token-empty pair, recovering the flash loan plus the pair's whole USDT reserve.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of the victim pair 0xf0b36389a12a28be1280c0ec2a4bbc76889d6a96, measured from its own balances: USDT 591841.327760739761309679 at block 112655389 and 181.576724119654205222 at block 112655390, a fall of exactly 591659.751036620107104457 USDT, which the receipt's Transfer logs confirm as 197050774.696543 USDT in and 197642434.447580 USDT out within the single exploit transaction. Attacker-supplied inputs are excluded by construction: the 197,050,832.75 USDT that entered the pair was flash-loaned campaign input and left again in the same transaction. Financing costs are not netted off, so the attacker's own realised profit is smaller: EOA 0x2677806d48325ced7533c54b86ed5e99b129a4ed went from 107.755447197024975180 to 578403.663035258025501958 USDT, a gain of 578295.907588061000526778 USDT, and the 13363.84 USDT difference is flash-loan and swap cost. Not valued: the 7997208.894795931 LULA the pair also lost, because the same transaction left the pair holding 181.58 USDT against 4749.05 LULA, so that quantity had no realisable value at any price and marking it would inflate the loss.

lastCodeChange.description: LULA is a plain Ownable contract with no proxy, no delegatecall and no self-destruct path. Its runtime hashes to 0x99366bf8f264505f8f861840792e1d39947be3cc92930adeb70dfcf4beefdb14 both at the deployment block 106133685 and at block 112655389 immediately before the exploit, so the recycle() implementation is unchanged over the whole interval.

The rental/reward contract is a non-upgradeable direct deployment whose runtime hashes to 0xcf4e6608ce8313103a4c0cf62f16f2e3f7d61c8146e50e71f9c9a83db3ce260c both at the deployment block 106134806 and at block 112655389 immediately before the exploit. It is the address LULA.rentalContract was fixed to and the only account recycle() accepts.

limitations: This target carries the same failureModeId as target-1 because it is the other half of one defect, so curve construction keeps only one observation for the incident and selects the earlier LULA deployment.

The rental contract's bytecode is not source-verified on BscScan. Its identity, runtime hash, deployment anchor and code-history completeness were reproduced onchain, and its role - a claimTeamReward() reachable by attacker-created contracts that unconditionally tops the payout up by calling LULA.recycle - was established from 41 successful iterations in the anchor call trace rather than from source.

sources.note: Anchor: 0xa219ab9d57e520e5235b15a8801f4ebac8cc45551be0430ce4e49caea0411d7c at 112655390:49, timestamp 1785254909, status 1; EOA 0x2677806d48325ced7533c54b86ed5e99b129a4ed calls its own helper 0x5e506ba06fa6c61d1069b0e68d7013de35afa816 (created eleven minutes earlier at block 112653941) with selector 0x763a0e5b. The attacker's earlier BSC transactions in the twelve days before are contract creations and reward registrations that accrue referral credit; they do not execute the confiscation, and there is no earlier successful transaction in which the pair is manipulated, so the campaign is this single transaction. Root cause read from the Etherscan-verified LULA source: `function recycle(uint256 amount) external { require(msg.sender == rentalContract, "Only Rental"); uint256 pairBalance = balanceOf[uniswapV2Pair]; uint256 maxTake = pairBalance / 3; uint256 actual = amount >= maxTake ? maxTake : amount; if (actual == 0) return; _basicTransfer(uniswapV2Pair, rentalContract, actual); IUniswapV2Pair(uniswapV2Pair).sync(); }`. Boundary test: the extraction cap is the hardcoded pairBalance/3 and there is no rate limit, no value bound and no check that the pair is not mid-manipulation; the only stored value recycle reads besides the pair balance is rentalContract, which initialize() fixes once behind `require(rentalContract == address(0))` with no setter, and which merely selects who may confiscate. No value of buyTaxRate, sellTaxRate, sellLpRate, swapAtAmount, swapSlippageBps, cooldownTime, lpPool or buyEnabled prevents the pair's reserve from being removed, so the deployed code is wrong for every configuration and this is an executable-code defect rather than the oracle-manipulation parameter case the legacy row implied. State read at block 112655389 confirms the wiring: LULA.rentalContract = 0x377a015f44c3fdf71060e94648edc9e0316c7f1a, LULA.uniswapV2Pair = 0xf0b36389a12a28be1280c0ec2a4bbc76889d6a96, LULA.owner = 0x43721abc1d19378c6160abfda6f1dd488ebbb5c9. Execution reproduced with cast run --quick: the helper takes recursive Moolah flash loans, swaps 197050832754852581075167541 USDT into the pair and routes the 7982785694934909976701260 LULA output to the fee-exempt owner address so _transfer takes the isExcludedFromFee branch and neither the 3 percent buy tax nor lastBuyTime is recorded, leaving the pair at 197642323.852857398857730617 USDT against 24022.129524779385677863 LULA; then 41 claimTeamReward() calls from attacker clones each reach 0x377a015f which calls LULA.recycle, and the receipt's Transfer logs show exactly 41 pair-to-rental LULA transfers totalling 24022.132677570768 LULA, each followed by pair.sync(); the recycled LULA is forwarded to the helper and sold back into the token-empty pair. Code history: Etherscan getcontractcreation puts LULA at 106133685:89 in 0xb1448a89b6b6c64876347aacaf95ebcda9a3309d47142c5cb766b5eb9da4f6de and the rental contract at 106134806:82 in 0x48b51c79ea25550d76b1550cbf63206f92ecc89dfaef5f4602c9d70e54293b49, both from 0x43721abc1d19378c6160abfda6f1dd488ebbb5c9, block timestamps 1782318652 and 1782319156 read from the chain; eth_getCode at the deployment blocks and at 112655389 gives 0x99366bf8f264505f8f861840792e1d39947be3cc92930adeb70dfcf4beefdb14 and 0xcf4e6608ce8313103a4c0cf62f16f2e3f7d61c8146e50e71f9c9a83db3ce260c unchanged, neither contract is a proxy, so codeAgeSeconds are 1785254909 - 1782318652 = 2936257 (34.0 d) and 1785254909 - 1782319156 = 2935753. Loss reconstructed from balances rather than from the reported figure: the pair's USDT went from 591841327760739761309679 to 181576724119654205222 wei, a depletion of 591659751036620107104457 wei, while the attacker EOA gained 578295907588061000526778 wei, which is the figure the legacy row and the public write-ups quote; the gross victim depletion is used here and the difference is financing cost.

notes: The legacy snapshot measured this row against the rental contract 0x377a015f44c3fdf71060e94648edc9e0316c7f1a (deployment timestamp 1782319156). Review keeps that contract as target-2 but the curve observation is selected on the LULA token, whose verified recycle() implementation contains the invariant violation and which was deployed 504 seconds earlier, so the measured age barely moves.

The victim is the PancakeSwap LULA/USDT pair 0xf0b36389a12a28be1280c0ec2a4bbc76889d6a96 and, through it, its liquidity providers. It is not itself a target: the pair executes standard Uniswap V2 code and its sync() behaves exactly as specified.
